context: Real-browser evidence showed XRBitcoin could enter an ambiguous Signing blocked state and route Connect Xaman into a reset confirmation. XRBitcoin and XRBitcoinCash use separate Xaman app IDs on the same origin while browser PKCE state uses the origin-scoped XummPkceJwt key. Passive browser restore could therefore adopt a cached session from the other app, fail application verification, and leave sessionFault set.

failure_chain: Browser setup passively restored cached account state.
Cached session could belong to the other Xaman application on the same origin.
sessionFault remained set and the candidate account/UI looked partially connected.
Connect routed into reset confirmation instead of starting a clean XRBitcoin authorization.
root_cause.classification: wallet session lifecycle defect; not pool/AMM read failure

repaired_states.disconnect: deterministic disconnected local state even if provider logout fails
repaired_states.wallet_details: explicit disconnected / connecting / reconnect required / connected status text

scenarios: Stale cross-project XummPkceJwt cache cleared before XRB authorization.
authorizeAndWarm starts authorization immediately and creates no transaction payload.
Connect uses the exact XRB Xaman application ID and no transaction construction path.
Provider logout failure still leaves the page locally disconnected.
Disconnect and reset are modal-free and preserve pending request storage.
Failed application verification cannot leave an accepted wallet account.
simulation.initial_test_result: failed because one assertion inspected setupSdk instead of the new wireSdk helper; production repair itself was not the failing assertion

preserve: XRBitcoin and XRBitcoinCash use separate Xaman application IDs.
Pending and ambiguous signing-request records survive disconnect/reset.
Validated XRPL finality, signer equality, intent/challenge binding and critical-field comparison remain required.
Exact XRB issuer/currency identity remains authoritative.
